articles.title: Paying an AI agent for work it hasn't delivered yet: bonded jobs on Solana, tried locally
articles.excerpt: x402 handles the simple case well: an agent pays, and gets a response right away. Many useful jobs do not fit that shape. A report, an export or a batch of lookups takes minutes, and the buyer pays be…
articles.body: x402 handles the simple case well: an agent pays, and gets a response right away. Many useful jobs do not fit that shape. A report, an export or a batch of lookups takes minutes, and the buyer pays before it can see the result. Agent402 Bond is a small Solana program for that gap. For one deal, the seller locks a bond and the buyer can lock a deposit. What happens to that money depends only on the two parties' signatures and the Solana clock. There is no arbiter and no operator who can move the funds. This post shows how to try it with your own AI agent (Claude Code or any MCP client) on a local fork of Solana mainnet. It uses throwaway keys and fork-only USDC, so nothing real is spent. It takes about five minutes.

articles.title: The poison is in the parameters: a labelled test set for MCP tool scanners
articles.excerpt: An MCP client hands the model a tool's whole definition: the name, the description, and the JSON schema for every parameter. The model reads all of it. So an instruction can hide anywhere in that sche…
articles.body: An MCP client hands the model a tool's whole definition: the name, the description, and the JSON schema for every parameter. The model reads all of it. So an instruction can hide anywhere in that schema, not only in the line a human skims in a tool list. Invariant Labs described this class publicly in 2025 as tool poisoning , and the OWASP MCP Top 10 lists it as MCP03. Benchmarks such as MCPTox measure how often agents follow poisoned tools. I published a small set for the step before that, the scanner: MCP Tool Poisoning Fixtures , 23 labelled rows on Hugging Face, Apache-2.0. Every poisoned field is labelled, and every poisoned tool has a clean twin. Where the poison sits Here is one poisoned tool from the set.

articles.title: GitHub Enterprise Server's Pre-Receive Hook Boundary Broke Under a Crafted Download URL
articles.excerpt: GitHub Enterprise Server's Pre-Receive Hook Boundary Broke Under a Crafted Download URL GitHub Enterprise Server administrators already hold broad control over a repository appliance. CVE-2026-112740…
articles.body: GitHub Enterprise Server's Pre-Receive Hook Boundary Broke Under a Crafted Download URL GitHub Enterprise Server administrators already hold broad control over a repository appliance. CVE-2026-112740 matters because the attacker could move from that administrative role into command execution as the host git user on a peer Git server node, outside the pre-receive hook sandbox. The condition is narrow. The advisory says exploitation required a clustered deployment that used custom pre-receive hook environments and included at least one peer Git server node. A crafted pre-receive environment download URL supplied the injection point. This was not a general unauthenticated request path. The boundary that failed Pre-receive environments are part of the hook execution system.

articles.title: The hour before a test run that nobody plans for
articles.excerpt: It's 10 minutes before you start testing the new checkout flow in UAT. You open the shared spreadsheet of test logins. The UAT row says checkout_user_02. The note next to it says "maybe expired?". It…
articles.body: It's 10 minutes before you start testing the new checkout flow in UAT. You open the shared spreadsheet of test logins. The UAT row says checkout_user_02 . The note next to it says "maybe expired?". It was last updated four months ago by someone who has since left. You try it. Locked. You ask in the team chat: "anyone have a working UAT login that can reach checkout?" Two people reply with two different accounts. One of them is already in use by someone else's test run. The other works, but it has no saved card, so you can't get past payment. Forty minutes later you're finally testing. Nobody planned for those forty minutes. They happen every sprint. This isn't a tooling gap. It's a missing source of truth. Most teams have solved generating test data.

articles.title: A different perspective on text, information and knowledge
articles.excerpt: We now produce more text than anyone can read. Agent instructions, specifications, pipelines, models, requirements, notes, and more and more of it written by AI. Most of it has a shape: a hierarchy, a…
articles.body: We now produce more text than anyone can read. Agent instructions, specifications, pipelines, models, requirements, notes, and more and more of it written by AI. Most of it has a shape: a hierarchy, a feedback loop, a flow, a web of dependencies. Plain text hides that shape, and a generic whiteboard flattens it. As AI writes more of it and the systems we build grow more tangled, reading it line by line stops scaling. That is the idea behind ADP, A Different Perspective : an open-source (Apache-2.0) family of tools that open the files you already keep in a view made for the question you have, and write every edit back as plain text. The same file, the right view Take a Markdown file that tells an AI agent how to behave. As text it is a nested bullet list.

articles.title: How to decode a JWT in Python (and what decoding does not prove)
articles.excerpt: How to decode a JWT in Python (and what decoding does not prove) Read any token with the stdlib or PyJWT, then see exactly where decoding stops and verifying starts. TL;DR The stdlib decode is a split…
articles.body: How to decode a JWT in Python (and what decoding does not prove) Read any token with the stdlib or PyJWT, then see exactly where decoding stops and verifying starts. TL;DR The stdlib decode is a split, a padding line, base64.urlsafe_b64decode and json.loads . The padding line is what most snippets omit. To inspect a token, call jwt.decode_complete(token, options={"verify_signature": False}) . To act on one, call jwt.decode with the key, algorithms= , audience= and issuer= . A hand-built alg: none token claiming role: admin decodes cleanly, and an HS256 allowlist refuses it with InvalidAlgorithmError . exp is epoch seconds in UTC, so compare it with time.time() . To decode a JWT in Python, you split it on the dots, restore the = padding that base64url dropped, and parse the result as JSON.

articles.title: Agentic RAG: grade the search, rewrite, retry with a cap
articles.excerpt: Agentic RAG lets an agent decide when and how to retrieve information while preparing an answer. We tested one design: grade the retrieved results, rewrite a failed query and retry within a cap. In ou…
articles.body: Agentic RAG lets an agent decide when and how to retrieve information while preparing an answer. We tested one design: grade the retrieved results, rewrite a failed query and retry within a cap. In our simulation run on 2026-11-15, one search found the right page for 20 of 40 questions, a cap of 2 searches found 32 and a cap of 4 found 38. Every extra round cost about 1.2 modeled seconds and a few hundred tokens, and the fourth round rescued nothing. Why one search misses: everyday words, technical pages {#miss} You type "Why does the site keep forgetting that I signed in?" The help page that answers it is titled "Session cookie expiry". None of your words appear on that page, so a keyword search ranks other pages above it.

articles.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
articles.excerpt: Conspiracy theories surround the odd-looking appearance of a shadow seen in the final images captured by Phobos 2, the Soviet Union’s last mission into deep space.
articles.body: On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft.

articles.body: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service to install malware on some customer routers and KVM devices, the maker of travel routers and remote-access KVM hardware said in a security notice updated today.
